gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-almendra-sc: Balsamiq Sans draws every curve with parallel edges and no pinched corners, bold and loose. And Almendra SC, a dignified serif with mouths that stay open, gives that looseness a more formal, small-capped partner.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-antic-slab: Stencil-channel lines, one weight throughout, mark Balsamiq Sans. It makes the loud, rounded statement, while the text serif Antic Slab does the quieter editorial work with sturdy bowls and wide s curves.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-belgrano: Marker-bold up top, traditional below. Balsamiq Sans keeps every stroke the same gauge, so Belgrano, a text serif with open curves, feels like the steadier, more classic voice when the text runs on.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-biorhyme: Expressive and bold, Balsamiq Sans has no thick-to-thin shading at all. It earns its keep big and short, while BioRhyme, a text serif, brings brush-lifted curve ends and widely spaced capitals.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-biorhyme-expande: Bent-tubing letters in Balsamiq Sans, all one gauge, set against BioRhyme Expanded, a refined serif with gaps that split words into single letters. Loose meets bookish.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-biz-udmincho: Loud, rounded and hand-built, Balsamiq Sans has crossbars matching its stems exactly. But BIZ UDMincho, a bookish serif with shallow terminal curls and wide gaps, wants a body size that lets those gaps breathe.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-copse: Chunky rounded rods, bold and playful, all in one weight from Balsamiq Sans. Copse, a literary serif with daylight in every curve, then reads smoothly.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-cutive: Bold, hand-drawn and shade-free, Balsamiq Sans has no calligraphic shading to guide the eye. Yet Cutive, a refined serif with wide tracking and generous openings, carries the reading with a typewriter-like quiet.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-enriqueta: Diagonals as thick as horizontals give Balsamiq Sans its bold, bent-wire look, and Enriqueta, a dignified serif with chalky curves that stop before closing, softens it. They suit each other well.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-fenix: Expressive, loud and loose. Balsamiq Sans does its best work with pencil-line consistency in big letters, while Fenix, a classic serif with curves ending before they turn inward, handles the editorial reading.
